newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. refugee chief hits Zaire over expulsions.
newsitem.headline: U.N. refugee chief hits Zaire over expulsions.

text.p: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata rejected on Monday allegations by Zaire's government that her agency's withdrawal from refugee camps in the country had led to thousands of deaths.
In a statement from UNHCR headquarters in Geneva, she also described Zaire's expulsion of 40 U.N. relief workers who pulled out of the eastern city of Kisangani as "both unfair and unjustified."
But she said the agency was planning to resume relief operations in government and rebel-held areas of the country.

On March 4 Zaire ordered the expulsion of the 40 U.N. and 17 other relief workers from non-governmental organisations who had left Kisangani saying declining security and harassment by the Zairean army made it impossible for them to work.
It said the withdrawal from Kisangani, and from the Tingi Tingi camp in eastern Zaire where mainly Rwandan refugees lived, had led to the slaughter by rebels of 25,000 people.
Ogata said the allegation was "simply groundless." She said the UNHCR knew of no credible reports to substantiate the claim that 25,000 people had died after rebel forces took control of the area.

She also rejected Zairean assertions that the aid workers had left the region for no good reason, saying local military authorities advised them in late February that their security could not be assured in the face of the rebel advance.

The Zaire government had failed to extend its own safe conduct passes issued to the aid workers, she said, and the Zairean army had requisitioned U.N.-chartered relief aircraft "further compromising both the relief operation and the security of humanitarian personnel."
